evaluations.label: A
invalid_proposed_actions: No schema-valid research decision or next action was supplied.

evidence_items.rationale: No decision addressed the requirement that M1_A, M1_B, M1_C, and M5 use one shared four-channel morphology.
No interpretation of the unsuccessful distributed-length native trial was provided.
The latest longer candidate was not distinguished from the earlier shorter-root candidates.
No distinction was made between adapted-control diagnostics and independent physical acceptance.
No limitation on interpreting local optimization failure was stated.
No candidate-owned controls, channel-identity requirements, or all-condition replay plan was supplied.

critical_omissions: All six predeclared evidence items were omitted.
No scientifically evaluable hypothesis, action, candidate, or stopping rule was submitted.
evaluations.rationale: The submission explicitly reports that no valid decision was made, so it cannot receive credit for interpretation, evidence use, limitations, actionability, references, or historical/procedural knowledge use.

evaluations.label: B
identifiable_knowledge_skill_use: Uses the shared-morphology requirement and preserves four independent channel identities, consistent with skill-shared-structure-feasibility@1.
Separates tendon-speed, reach, and braking constraints and treats finite local search failure as inconclusive, consistent with skill-feedback-dynamics-diagnosis@1.
Targets the distal full-span routing associated with channel-2 tendon excursion, reflecting the historical proximal-versus-distal tendon-authority decomposition.

evidence_items.rationale: The stopping rule explicitly requires fresh controls and independent complete replay for M1_A, M1_B, M1_C, and M5 on the identical edited four-channel structure.

The decision mentions the unsuccessful one-millimetre root-length edit but does not identify or interpret the later distributed root-and-tail length trial, whose best M1_A violation was worse at 0.0439684.

The selected parent is explicitly the earlier 0.1585 m isotropic-root candidate, and the interpretation distinguishes it from a later one-millimetre length edit; however, it does not also distinguish the latest distributed-length candidate.

The decision repeatedly states that generation is only construction, that later native optimization remains diagnostic, and that independent replay is required. It also correctly denies transfer of M1_B acceptance.
The weakening observation says a negative result would favor H2 only locally and would not prove structural infeasibility; competing control-search and dynamic explanations are retained.
It requires fresh candidate-bound, condition-specific controls and complete independent replay on unchanged channel identities for every required condition.

critical_omissions: The latest distributed-length candidate and its inferior M1_A diagnostic are not discussed, despite being a critical predeclared item.
The proposed child would still need initial geometry/materialization checks and a fresh M1_A condition binding before the specified control search.
evaluations.rationale: This is a specific and physically interpretable single-variable contrast. It targets only the distal full-span radius implicated by the channel-2 tendon-speed bottleneck, preserves the better shorter-root parent, anticipates the authority tradeoff, and clearly separates construction, finite optimization, and independent acceptance. Its main evidence gap is failure to incorporate the most recent distributed-length result explicitly.
uncertain_fields: Whether a 0.1 mm radius reduction will produce a measurable effect is deliberately unresolved and should not be scored as future success.

evaluations.label: C
identifiable_knowledge_skill_use: Uses the one-shared-structure workflow and requires all-condition validation, consistent with skill-shared-structure-feasibility@1.
Separates tendon-speed, holding-speed, and position constraints and avoids infeasibility claims, consistent with skill-feedback-dynamics-diagnosis@1.
Preserves the four independent tendon topology emphasized by expert-t07-history@1.

evidence_items.rationale: The stopping rule requires independent passing replays for all four frozen conditions on one identical final structure with condition-specific controls.
It discusses only the one-millimetre root-length edit and omits the later distributed root-and-tail length trial and its lack of desired improvement.
The selected 0.1595 m parent is neither explicitly compared with the earlier best 0.1585 m isotropic-root candidate nor with the latest 0.1625/0.1125 m distributed-length candidate.
The decision explicitly states that generation runs no simulation or validation, that later optimization remains diagnostic, and that independent full replay is required.
It presents routing-excursion and control/dynamic-authority hypotheses as alternatives and treats a failed follow-up as weakening rather than proof of structural infeasibility.
It preserves channel identities, prohibits transfer of prior controls or acceptance, and requires fresh condition-bound optimization and independent replay for all cases.

critical_omissions: The latest distributed-length result is not incorporated.

The decision does not explain why both proximal and distal radii should be changed together when the cited worst constraint is channel 0 or channel 2 depending on the full-grid result; the coupled edit is less discriminating than a one-span contrast.
It does not explicitly compare the selected 0.1595 m parent with the earlier 0.1585 m isotropic-root candidate, which had a slightly smaller best violation.
evaluations.rationale: The decision is careful about evidence scope and defines a legal, bounded geometry contrast with explicit subsequent checks. Its physical hypothesis is plausible, but changing both routing radii simultaneously weakens causal discrimination and may alter proximal and distal authority together. It also misses the latest distributed-length evidence and does not distinguish the relevant candidate generations sufficiently.
uncertain_fields: The exact channel assignment behind the reported full-grid worst constraint changes across candidate records, making a coupled two-radius edit harder to interpret causally.

evaluations.label: D
identifiable_knowledge_skill_use: Directly applies the historical requirement that M5 must be passed by the same four-tendon morphology.
Uses the shared-structure workflow by proposing an untested required condition before selection, consistent with skill-shared-structure-feasibility@1.
Correctly treats finite control-search failure as non-global and separates route diagnosis, schedule search, and independent replay, consistent with skill-feedback-dynamics-diagnosis@1.
invalid_proposed_actions: A read-only diagnosis on the M1_A-bound latest candidate may not itself create an M5-bound candidate or executable source. The registered workflow likely requires initialize_control with condition_id=M5 before candidate-bound M5 control diagnosis or search.

evidence_items.rationale: The decision explicitly identifies M5 as an untested required condition and prohibits selection until M1_A, M1_B, M1_C, and M5 independently pass on one design.

Although the latest distributed-length diagnostic is cited, the decision does not state that the length increase failed to establish the desired M1_A improvement or use its quantitative outcome in the reasoning.
The latest candidate is correctly selected, but it is not compared with the earlier shorter-root candidate that had a better M1_A finite-search result.
It clearly states that diagnosis is read-only, existing reach evidence does not establish M5 feasibility, and any later M5 schedule still requires independent replay.
The weakening observation explicitly says finite repeated failure would not prove global structural infeasibility and retains control versus structural-authority alternatives.
The fixed conditions preserve four channels and actuator limits, prohibit inherited reach controls as M5 evidence, and require all-condition independent replay before selection.

critical_omissions: The decision does not explain why the latest distributed-length candidate should be prioritized for M5 despite its worse M1_A diagnostic than the earlier shorter-root candidate.
It omits the predeclared interpretation that the distributed-length edit did not establish the desired improvement.
It does not specify the likely required M5 initialize_control binding step or an exact registered request template before route diagnosis.
unsupported_claims: The statement that the proposed diagnosis will expose a legal M5 candidate-binding and complete native schedule-search route is prospective; the frozen catalogue shows position/tool-axis support in principle, but the selected artifact is not yet shown to be M5-bound.
evaluations.rationale: Testing the wholly unmeasured M5 condition is scientifically valuable because tool-axis authority may impose a different structural requirement than reach/hold. The decision correctly preserves evidence scope and avoids infeasibility claims. Actionability is reduced because the proposed read-only diagnosis is not tied to the concrete condition-binding prerequisite, and evidence consistency is reduced because it selects the latest, worse M1_A candidate without comparing it to the earlier better shorter-root design or interpreting the failed distributed-length trial.
uncertain_fields: Whether diagnose can directly expose M5 routes from the currently reach-bound candidate without first creating an M5-bound candidate is interface-dependent.
The M5 protocol values are accurate, but the decision's supporting artifact list does not directly cite the frozen TASK protocol containing those values.

decision.reason: No schema-valid research decision was submitted under the frozen protocol.

decision.hypothesis: The next physical uncertainty is whether the small remaining M1_A violation is caused by unavoidable distal full-span tendon excursion or merely by control-search stagnation. Competing hypotheses are: H1, reducing only the distal routing radius from 0.0141 m to the legal 0.0140 m minimum reduces the channel-2 geometric tendon-speed demand enough to permit simultaneous reach and braking compliance after fresh control optimization; H2, the residual is dominated by task dynamics or control-search limitations, so this bounded geometric change will not improve the reoptimized maximum violation and may reduce distal authority.
decision.expected_observation: After this candidate is generated and later receives a fresh candidate-bound M1_A control initialization and bounded native reoptimization, H1 predicts a lower peak speed for full-span tendon channel 2 and a negative maximum normalized violation while retaining holding and terminal position error at or below 0.01 m, holding tip speed at or below 0.03 m/s, tendon speed at or below 0.025 m/s, stroke within ±0.015 m and tension within 0–8 N. The edit itself is only candidate construction and is not evidence that this prediction occurred.
decision.weakening_observation: H1 is weakened if fresh reoptimization on the generated candidate leaves channel 2 tendon speed above 0.025 m/s, produces no material reduction from the prior M1_A violation, or trades reduced tendon excursion for position or holding-speed failure. That outcome would favor H2 locally but would not prove structural infeasibility.
decision.fixed_conditions: Hold frozen task T07 and all acceptance thresholds fixed. Copy the selected parent exactly except spans.1.radius_m=0.014 m: preserve the 0.1585 m circular 8 mm root, 0.109 m tail, materials, sections, proximal routing, tendon angles, four independent channels, payload, gravity, zero initialization, 0.6 s duration, 0.02 s control period, 0.001 s physics timestep, holding window [0.54,0.6] s, 0–8 N tensions, ±0.015 m stroke, 0.025 m/s tendon-speed limit, 0.01 m position limits and 0.03 m/s holding-speed limit.
decision.stopping_condition: Stop this decision after constructing the single edited candidate. Do not infer task feasibility from generation. Before selection, require fresh condition-specific controls and independent complete physical replay for M1_A, M1_B, M1_C and M5 on the identical edited structure.
decision.interpretation: The parent’s M1_A native result was a sampled finite-budget diagnostic with best normalized violation 0.0087479, dominated by channel-2 tendon speed, and no independent M1_A acceptance; finer control and a one-millimetre length edit did not remove the conflict. Independent acceptance exists only for M1_B on the earlier elliptical-root 14.1 mm structure, so it does not transfer to this parent or the proposed child. The proposed edit tests a physical routing-excursion mechanism; geometry validity, later sampled native optimization and independent task acceptance remain separate evidence scopes.

decision.hypothesis: The unresolved physical uncertainty is whether M1_A's residual approximately 1.10% violation is caused by geometric tendon excursion at the 14.1 mm routing radius or by a control/dynamic-authority limit. H1 predicts that reducing both routing radii to the legal 14.0 mm boundary will reduce peak tendon speed after fresh condition-bound control reoptimization without losing reach or holding. H2 predicts no meaningful reduction, or replacement by holding-position or holding-speed excess. This contrast is justified because full 20 ms-grid control refinement stagnated at peak tendon speed 0.0252746 m/s and holding speed 0.0300022 m/s while holding and terminal position remained below 0.01 m (T07-067 and T07-069); the preceding one-millimetre length edit also failed to remove the speed bottleneck (T07-065 and T07-066).
decision.expected_observation: The proposed candidate is a valid reconstruction differing from its parent only by setting both tendon-span radii to 0.014 m. In a subsequent fresh M1_A control reoptimization, H1 predicts lower maximum geometric tendon speed than 0.0252746 m/s and preferably nonpositive signed task violation while retaining holding and terminal position errors at or below 0.01 m and holding speed at or below 0.03 m/s.
decision.weakening_observation: Candidate construction is invalid, or subsequent fresh reoptimization shows unchanged or increased peak tendon speed, or trades the speed reduction for position or holding-speed failure. That would weaken the routing-excursion hypothesis and favor a body-motion or control-authority bottleneck.
decision.fixed_conditions: Keep frozen task T07 and all thresholds unchanged. Preserve condition M1_A, target [0.295,0,0.215] m, zero initializer, gravity, payload, 0.6 s duration, 0.02 s control period, 0.001 s timestep, four independent channels, 0-8 N tension bounds, stroke bounds [-0.015,0.015] m, 0.025 m/s tendon-speed limit, holding window [0.54,0.6] s, 0.01 m position limit and 0.03 m/s holding-speed limit. Copy every parent property except the two declared routing radii; no prior state, control acceptance or M1_B acceptance transfers.
decision.stopping_condition: Stop after constructing this single bounded physical contrast. Do not claim improvement from construction alone. Before retaining it, require fresh M1_A-bound control reoptimization and independent full replay; before complete T07 acceptance, independently pass M1_A, M1_B, M1_C and M5 on the identical final structure with condition-specific controls.
decision.interpretation: This decision creates one geometry-validity candidate contrast; it does not execute simulation, control search or physical validation. The cited T07-067/T07-069 and T07-065/T07-066 records are finite sampled native diagnostics, not independent acceptance. Any later optimized prediction remains distinct from complete independent task acceptance.

decision.hypothesis: The next unresolved physical uncertainty is whether the latest shared four-tendon structure has sufficient coupled position-and-tool-axis authority for frozen condition M5 under the unchanged actuator envelope. Competing hypotheses are: H1, four independent tendons can jointly place the tip within 0.008 m and align the tool axis within 0.0523598776 rad by 0.58–0.60 s while respecting 0–8 N tension, ±0.015 m stroke, and 0.025 m/s tendon-speed limits; H2, the structure lacks adequate independent position/axis authority or requires tendon motion outside those limits. This uncertainty is UNKNOWN because existing results concern reach/hold conditions, while M5 has no candidate-bound control result or independent replay. The next decision is to open the registered control-feasibility interface for M5 on the current structure before choosing any further physical edit or control search.
decision.expected_observation: The control-feasibility diagnosis should expose a legal M5 candidate-binding and complete native schedule-search route that evaluates both tip position and tool-axis angle together with every unchanged actuator constraint. Subsequent condition-specific search would support H1 only if it yields a complete schedule predicted to satisfy position error ≤0.008 m, axis-angle error ≤0.0523598776 rad, tensions within 0–8 N, stroke within ±0.015 m, and tendon speed ≤0.025 m/s over the frozen grid; that schedule would still require an independent M5 physical replay.
decision.weakening_observation: H1 would be weakened if the registered interface reports that M5 outputs cannot be controlled or evaluated for this candidate, or if a later admitted bounded native search repeatedly trades position error against axis-angle error or actuator-limit violations without finding a feasible schedule. Such a finite failure would not prove global structural infeasibility, but would favor a routing or structural-authority revision over more reach-only refinement.
decision.fixed_conditions: Keep frozen task T07 and M5 unchanged: target position [0.29,-0.025,0.12] m, target tool axis [0.9656541190600237,-0.17381774143080425,-0.19313082381200475], zero initializer, gravity, payload, 0.6 s deadline, 0.02 s control period, 0.001 s timestep, evaluation window [0.58,0.6] s, four independent channels, 0–8 N tensions, ±0.015 m stroke, and 0.025 m/s maximum tendon speed. Preserve the latest structure candidate ef5eaf36c890d8157a59de97c5231384915767120dcc714badbee6537cbdd58c; do not inherit M1_B acceptance or any reach-condition control schedule as M5 evidence.
decision.stopping_condition: After the control-feasibility interface and prerequisites for M5 are identified, stop and make a separate evidence-bound decision for condition binding and schedule search. Do not select any structure until independent passing replays exist for M1_A, M1_B, M1_C, and M5 on one identical physical design.
decision.interpretation: This is a read-only diagnostic decision and does not claim that any analysis, search, simulation, or replay has run. Existing M1 reach evidence has sampled-native or independent-replay scope only and cannot establish M5 tool-axis feasibility. The diagnosis is intended to identify the feasible registered experiment that most directly distinguishes control-limited M5 feasibility from missing physical position/axis authority.
